reference.title: Reference-informed synthetic senior care scenarios

source.title: MITRE Synthea April 2020 sample CSV
source.reuse: Official download page states data is free from cost, privacy and security restrictions.

reference.basis: Blood pressure, non-diabetes glucose and body-weight reference distributions come from per-person medians in the public MITRE Synthea sample at observation age 60-110. Every identity and daily signal below is newly simulated.
authoredAssumptions: Eight percent of identities receive deliberately planted review scenarios for stress testing; this is not a prevalence estimate.
Daily serial correlation, measurement schedules, symptom wording, medication-taking, activity and sleep are authored assumptions.
The reference is synthetic US EHR data, not an Indian geriatric or longitudinal home-care outcomes cohort.
SpO2 and treatment-history subgroups are illustrative because compatible reference observations are unavailable.
reference.validation: Data-quality and synthetic identity-held-out checks; no patient-outcome validation or diagnostic probabilities.

systolic.aggregation: One median per synthetic identity at observation age 60-110; distribution across identity medians.

diastolic.aggregation: One median per synthetic identity at observation age 60-110; distribution across identity medians.

glucose.aggregation: One median per synthetic identity at observation age 60-110; distribution across identity medians.

weight.aggregation: One median per synthetic identity at observation age 60-110; distribution across identity medians.

spo2.reason: No compatible observations in this reference archive.

quality.interpretation: Passing structural and consistency checks does not validate physiological realism, representativeness, risk thresholds or clinical outcomes. Broad bounds are input plausibility checks, not reference ranges or treatment advice.

metrics.leadTimeMeaning: Planted escalation is a synthetic review deadline, not an observed acute event or the start of decline.

model.name: Isolation Forest + personal-baseline rules
model.reference: Liu, Ting & Zhou (2008), Isolation Forest, IEEE ICDM. https://doi.org/10.1109/ICDM.2008.17
model.training: Unlabelled observations from each development identity’s first 30 days. Every fourth identity is held out from forest fitting. Baseline warm-up returns unknown priority; no labels fit the forest.
model.nlp: Local, hand-authored Hindi / English / Hinglish cue lexicon with bounded negation handling; no external language model or speech service.
model.dataset: Reference-informed synthetic senior care scenarios; aggregate source SHA256 4194b18c11eaedcf0d5d5dd448d8ac9661f14381e2ef9f109215dc42266cd38a
model.limitations: Data-quality and synthetic identity-held-out checks; no patient-outcome validation or diagnostic probabilities.

metrics.methodology: The same Isolation Forest and personal-baseline rules are fitted on first-30-day development identities and evaluated on identity-held-out days31 onward. Positive annotations cover deliberately authored review scenarios including persistent changes during gradual recovery. Other days are unlabelled, not adjudicated healthy. Daily coverage and case coverage describe these synthetic scenarios only. Clinical precision, specificity, F1 and predictive accuracy cannot be estimated; high flags outside annotated windows are reported as unlabelled high days, not false alarms. Scenario labels never enter model fitting.

ablation.comparison: Same cohort, split, dates, thresholds, NLP and rules; only the anomaly contribution is disabled.

scenarioReviewCoverage.meaning: A high or medium priority prompts a human check-in; distinct from threshold-60 high-priority coverage.

metrics.evaluatedAnnotationScope: Positive authored review scenarios only; other days are unlabelled.
metrics.recallLabel: Daily high-flag coverage within authored review scenarios
metrics.precisionLabel: Not estimable: unlabelled days are not confirmed negatives

clinicalPerformance.reason: No independent patient outcomes or adjudicated negative days are available.
